_about: Maple Grove's townsfolk (Alex, 2026-11-17): people with no part in the story, there to make the town feel alive (scripts/townsfolk.gd). They wander the town, sit on its benches, drop into the Cappuccino Cafe to read, and go home at dusk. Talking to one gets a single short line, picked from 'lines' by who they are (a line's 'who' lists the tags a speaker must have; none means anyone). Some days one wants a sweater ('want_chance'): a red pin bobs over their head and Nora can sell them one with the haggle panel. 'people' are also character entries for Body.load_character (Data.character falls back to this file): 'model' is the rigged model, the anim speeds are already multiplied by 'scale' (the model is rigged at a grown-up's height and shrunk in the game for the children). 'max_out' caps how many are about at once, 'hours' is when the town is out (each person keeps their own hours inside it), 'exits' are where they leave town at dusk (until Bretton Oaks gives them houses: townsfolk.gd home_spot()). Names, lines and numbers are drafts until Alex approves them.

lines.text: I hope my wife forgives me... maybe I'll buy her flowers.
Why are you always walking around? Don't you have a job?
Hey, um... do I know you?
Don't look at the clock on the town hall for too long. It looks back.
I counted the benches in the square this morning. There's one more than yesterday.
My mum says never talk to people carrying knitting needles.
If anyone asks, I was at the bakery all afternoon.
The ducks know something. I'm sure of it.
I left the oven on in 1998. I keep meaning to go back.
Shh. I'm practising being invisible. Is it working?
Lovely weather. Unless you know what's coming.
You smell like sheep. That's not a complaint.
I lost a button somewhere in this town last spring. I'm still looking.

want_lines: Is that a sweater you're carrying? I've been after one all week.
You knit? I could do with something warm.
